blocks.orig: Finding the right spot for perfect pictures can be tricky. With local guides and a special jeep for photographic safaris, you head out to capture unique nature, culture and wildlife scenes for eternity.
blocks.html: Knowing where to stand for the perfect shot is not always easy. Together with local guides, and in a jeep adapted for photographic safaris, you set out to record remarkable scenes of nature, culture and wildlife that will last a lifetime.

blocks.orig: First on your photographic safari agenda: a visit to the Tarangire National Park, home of the elephants. During a day and night game drive, you meet both diurnal and nocturnal animals. After this first exhilarating experience, you discover the green oasis of Mto Wa Mbu in a tuk-tuk as well as the scenic Lake Manyara National Park. A mix of stunning landscapes and fascinating culture awaits you next – with the Hadzabe tribe and Lake Eyasi, as well as a visit to a Maasai village and the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. Keep your eyes open and your camera on standby, since the Big Five and countless other African animals roam this special speck of land.
blocks.html: Your photographic safari opens in Tarangire National Park, the land of the elephants. On a game drive by day and another after dark, you come across animals that are active in daylight as well as those that come out at night. Once this thrilling start is behind you, a tuk-tuk takes you through Mto Wa Mbu, a green oasis, before you explore the picturesque Lake Manyara National Park. Next comes a blend of striking scenery and intriguing culture: the Hadzabe tribe and Lake Eyasi, followed by a Maasai village and the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. Stay alert and keep your camera ready, because the Big Five and a great many other African animals live on this remarkable patch of land.

blocks.orig: You continue to the (in)famous Serengeti, crossing it from central west to east by 4×4 and a hot air balloon: as the sun rises slowly, you take off into the sky, and the animals of the endless plains begin to stir, creating a scene so beautiful, only nature can paint it. Perfect for pictures you will cherish forever.
blocks.html: From there you travel on to the (in)famous Serengeti, which you cross from the central west to the east by 4×4 and by hot air balloon: while the sun slowly comes up, you lift off, and below you the animals of the endless plains start to wake, a picture so lovely that only nature could create it. Ideal for photos you will treasure for ever.

blocks.orig: The Serengeti also sets the stage for the Great Wildebeest Migration. During this spectacle, millions of wildebeest and zebras gallop towards greener pastures. If you go to Tanzania at the right time, you can travel to the Ndutu region, where new life is brought into this world during the wildebeest calving season.
blocks.html: The Great Wildebeest Migration also plays out in the Serengeti. In this spectacle, millions of zebras and wildebeest race off in search of greener grazing. Travel to Tanzania at the right moment and you can visit the Ndutu region, where the wildebeest calving season brings new life into the world.

blocks.orig: No matter if you want to capture the most colourful birds or the captivating gaze of a lion – this photographic safari will provide you with the perfect setting.
blocks.html: Whether your goal is to photograph the brightest birds or the piercing stare of a lion, this photographic safari gives you the ideal backdrop.

blocks.orig: Many travelers ask us when the best time is to visit Tanzania. The answer is … there is not one right answer. It depends on what you want to see, where you want to go, your budget and interests. Please find a comprehensive guide on when is the best time to visit Tanzania here.
blocks.html: A question we hear a lot is when you should travel to Tanzania. Honestly, no single answer fits everyone. It comes down to what you hope to see, where you would like to go, your budget and what interests you. You can read our detailed guide on the best time to visit Tanzania here.

blocks.orig: Our safaris in Tanzania offer an opportunity to explore the country’s incredible wildlife and stunning landscapes. We specialize in private safaris, which means you have a 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep all to yourselves. You have the flexibility to decide when the safari starts and ends, and our experienced guides can help you make that decision on the day of your adventure. Whether you want to witness the animals at their most active during sunrise and sunset when temperatures are pleasant, or if you fancy ending the day by the pool, it’s entirely up to you. Tanzania’s diverse wildlife is active at various times of the day, so you’ll have plenty of opportunities to spot the animals in action.
blocks.html: With our safaris in Tanzania you get the chance to discover the country’s remarkable wildlife and beautiful scenery. Private safaris are our speciality, so the 4×4 Landcruiser or jeep is reserved just for you and your companions. You choose when each safari day begins and finishes, and on the day itself our experienced guides are happy to help you decide. Would you like to see the animals when they are most active, at sunrise and sunset while it is still pleasantly cool, or would you rather finish the afternoon at the pool? That choice is completely yours. Because Tanzania’s varied wildlife is active at different times of day, you’ll get many chances to watch the animals in action.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is renowned as one of the prime destinations to encounter the Big Five. These magnificent creatures—lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros, and buffalo—can be observed in their natural habitats, making Tanzania a preferred choice for wildlife enthusiasts.
blocks.html: Certainly. Tanzania is known as one of the best places to see the Big Five. Lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros and buffalo, these impressive animals, can all be seen in their natural surroundings, which is why so many wildlife lovers choose Tanzania.

blocks.orig: Absolutely, Tanzania is a safe and welcoming destination for travelers. The country offers a hospitable environment, especially in tourist areas like Arusha, and you can explore its beautiful landscapes and wildlife with confidence. Local people are friendly, and safety measures, such as keeping an eye on your belongings, are always advisable, just as you would in any other part of the world. Tanzania’s natural beauty and the warmth of its people make it a fantastic place to visit.
blocks.html: Certainly. Tanzania is a welcoming and safe country for travellers. You will find a hospitable atmosphere, particularly in tourist areas such as Arusha, and you can enjoy its lovely scenery and wildlife with peace of mind. People are friendly, and as anywhere else in the world it is sensible to take basic precautions, such as watching your belongings. With its natural beauty and warm-hearted people, Tanzania is a wonderful place to travel to.

blocks.html: The moment you step out of Kilimanjaro International Airport, your own Your Tanzania Trip guide welcomes you with a broad smile: 'Karibu Tanzania - welcome to Tanzania!' You are driven directly to your hotel, where you can unwind and soak up the African atmosphere. blocks.orig: Tarangire National Park is well known for its big groups of elephants and the huge amount of giant baobab trees. These trees can live for hundreds of years and are actually a source of water for elephants in the dry season as they have a special technique to draw water from them. Besides, the Tarangire River is the only source of water in the dry season, which is why in this season in Tarangire you can see groups of up to 250 elephants next to many more animals!
blocks.html: Tarangire National Park is famous for its large herds of elephants and its great number of giant baobab trees. These baobabs can reach an age of several hundred years, and in the dry season elephants actually rely on them for water, using a special technique to get it out. On top of that, the Tarangire River is the only water source during the dry season, so at that time of year you can see herds of as many as 250 elephants in Tarangire, along with plenty of other animals!

blocks.orig: Experience the thrill of a night game drive in Tarangire National Park during your stay at Tarangire Safari Lodge. As twilight descends, venture into the wild and witness the vibrant nightlife of the African savanna. With expert guides leading the way, discover unique nocturnal wildlife and the mesmerizing sounds of nature. This unforgettable adventure allows you to see Tarangire’s diverse ecosystems in a new light. Don’t miss your chance to explore the wonders of Tanzania beneath the stars! Book your night game drive now!
blocks.html: While you stay at Tarangire Safari Lodge, enjoy the excitement of a night game drive in Tarangire National Park. When dusk falls, head out into the wild and see the lively nightlife of the African savanna for yourself. Led by expert guides, you discover special nocturnal animals and the enchanting sounds of nature. This memorable outing shows you Tarangire’s varied ecosystems in a whole new light. Take the opportunity to explore Tanzania’s wonders under the stars! Reserve your night game drive now!

blocks.orig: Lake Manyara National Park lies between Tarangire National Park and the Ngorongoro Crater, right along the 400 meters deep Great Rift Valley. The park boasts a variety of landscapes that attract many different animals. You can for example visit the lake that covers 75 percent of the park, pass through a dense rainforest with hundreds of monkeys and birds, and see elephants up close in the woodlands.
blocks.html: Between Tarangire National Park and the Ngorongoro Crater lies Lake Manyara National Park, right beside the Great Rift Valley, which is 400 meters deep. The park has a range of landscapes that draw many different animals. You can, for instance, visit the lake, which takes up 75 percent of the park, walk through a thick rainforest full of hundreds of monkeys and birds, and watch elephants at close range in the woodlands.

blocks.orig: The village of Mto wa Mbu is a green oasis in between dry savannah plains, close to Lake Manyara National Park. A tuktuk can take a maximum of 3 people and a tour by tuktuk allows for maximum flexibility. Tuktuks can pass through small streets and can stop anywhere you like. The tour leads past the village itself, then into the forest and past several farms and plantations. In one or two hours you will stop at a brewery, a local artist and a local school.
blocks.html: Close to Lake Manyara National Park, the village of Mto wa Mbu forms a green oasis amid dry savannah plains. Each tuktuk seats no more than 3 people, and touring by tuktuk gives you as much flexibility as possible. They fit through narrow streets and can stop wherever you want. The route takes you past the village, then into the forest and along a number of farms and plantations. Over one or two hours you call in at a brewery, a local artist and a local school.

blocks.orig: A visit to Lake Eyasi and the resident Hadzabe tribe makes for a fascinating daytrip. Lake Eyasi is a seasonal shallow salt lake south of the Ngorongoro Highlands, and a paradise for bird lovers. Spot hippos in the shallow waters, then take out your binoculars to spot for example the African spoonbill, flamingos, gray headed gulls, great white pelicans and pied avocets. Then visit the Hadzabe bushmen, masters in bow hunting.
blocks.html: A day trip to Lake Eyasi and the Hadzabe tribe who live there is a fascinating experience. South of the Ngorongoro Highlands, Lake Eyasi is a shallow, seasonal salt lake and a haven for birdwatchers. Look for hippos in the shallows, then reach for your binoculars to find species such as the African spoonbill, flamingos, gray headed gulls, great white pelicans and pied avocets. Afterwards you meet the Hadzabe bushmen, who are experts at hunting with a bow.

blocks.orig: The famous Ngorongoro Crater is one of Africa's seven natural wonders. The crater was formed two million years ago when a vast volcano erupted. The fertile lava has created a unique ecosystem, now home to the highest concentration of animals found anywhere in Africa! Once in the crater, thousands of animals such as lions, zebras, buffalos and black rhinos surround you, and the views are astounding – you won’t know where to look!
blocks.html: The well-known Ngorongoro Crater counts as one of Africa's seven natural wonders. It came into being two million years ago, when an enormous volcano erupted. Its fertile lava gave rise to a unique ecosystem that now holds the highest concentration of animals anywhere in Africa! Inside the crater you are surrounded by thousands of animals, including lions, zebras, buffalos and black rhinos, and the scenery is so astonishing you won’t know which way to look!

blocks.orig: Immerse yourself in the culture, colors, and traditions of the Maasai, go on a journey through time and experience how people can be satisfied with the simplest way of life. Learn about their survival skills and what their everyday life looks like in and around their village homes. A unique experience you don't want to miss during your Tanzania trip!
blocks.html: Dive into the culture, colours and traditions of the Maasai, travel back in time and see how people can find contentment in the simplest way of living. Discover their survival skills and what daily life is like in and around the homes of their village. It is a special experience that deserves a place in your Tanzania trip!

blocks.orig: Serengeti National Park is widely known as the place to go on safari, mainly because of the Great Migration that passes through here. The enormous, stampeding herds are impressive, as are the vast number of predators that live here: over four thousand lions, over 200 cheetahs, a thousand leopards, 3500 hyenas, and hundreds of wild dogs! And of course, plenty of other beautiful animals, which your guide will be delighted to search for together with you. Are you ready for this?
blocks.html: Serengeti National Park is famous as the safari destination, largely thanks to the Great Migration moving through it. The huge thundering herds are a sight to behold, and so is the sheer number of predators that live here: more than four thousand lions, more than 200 cheetahs, a thousand leopards, 3500 hyenas and hundreds of wild dogs! There are of course many other lovely animals too, and your guide will be glad to look for them with you. Are you ready?

blocks.orig: A balloon safari in the iconic Serengeti National Park will make your Tanzania safari a memorable experience. You rise at sunrise and gently fly over the endless plains of the Serengeti. The hot air balloon floats at treetop height above the baobabs and acacias so that you can see the animals nearby. Watching the wildlife below from your balloon is a fascinating and peaceful experience that comes with breathtaking panoramic views.
blocks.html: Taking a balloon safari over the iconic Serengeti National Park turns your Tanzania safari into an experience to remember. You go up as the sun rises and drift softly above the endless Serengeti plains. The hot air balloon glides at the height of the treetops, over the baobabs and acacias, so the animals are close by. Seeing the wildlife beneath your balloon is both captivating and calm, and the panoramic views are breathtaking.

blocks.orig: From late December through March, the Ndutu region becomes the heart of the Great Migration, as over 2 million animals arrive to give birth. The Ndutu region straddles the southern part of the Serengeti and the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. The short, nutrient-rich grass makes the area a haven for newborn zebras and wildebeests, but also a prime spot for predators. This seasonal gathering creates close-up wildlife sightings and constant activity across the plains.
blocks.html: Between late December and March, the Ndutu region is at the centre of the Great Migration, when more than 2 million animals come here to give birth. Ndutu stretches across the southern Serengeti and the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. Its short grass, rich in nutrients, makes it a safe haven for newborn wildebeests and zebras, yet also an ideal hunting ground for predators. This seasonal gathering brings close-up sightings and nonstop activity across the plains.

Having second thoughts? It's also possible to add a few days to your holiday by going to one of Tanzania's paradise islands, such as Zanzibar, Pemba, or Mafia!
blocks.html: Your final day! Depending on when your flight leaves, you can spend a little more time relaxing at the lodge before you go to Kilimanjaro International Airport (JRO) for the flight home. Not quite ready to leave? You can also extend your holiday by a few days on one of Tanzania's paradise islands, such as Zanzibar, Pemba or Mafia!
